questions.q: In "What makes a good call Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Remove clutter from the background or use a plain wall.
Say what you are doing; give a plan B.
Record only after announcing it and getting consent.
Place the camera at eye level using books if needed.

questions.q: In "Tools and rooms Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: Choose microphone and speaker; check levels.
Test the microphone level by speaking at normal volume and watching the meter.
Passcodes and locked rooms for private meetings.
Lost data packets (small chunks of data) cause choppy sound.

questions.q: In "Audio and video setup Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Place the camera at eye level using books if needed.
Say what you are doing; give a plan B.
Choose microphone and speaker; check levels.
Save the participants' names for the thank-you note.

questions.q: In "Network and quality Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Time each part against the run sheet.
Name your screen with your role, for example 'Host, your first name'.
Practise muting and unmuting others politely.
Keep a backup route ready, such as a second link or a phone number, and share it in the invite so a failed room costs two minutes rather than the whole session.

questions.q: In "Access and inclusion Analyse", which of these is a key idea?
o: Open the tool on a phone as a guest to see what attendees see.
Allow chat as well as voice.
Log the fault and cure.
Check accessibility settings such as caption language.

questions.q: In "Run the session Create", which of these is a key idea?
o: Ask attendees for a score and one comment.
Open the room 10 minutes early; greet people as they arrive.
Fallback: turn off video, then call in by phone.
Common: no sound, frozen picture, wrong room, someone cannot join.

questions.q: In "Fix problems live Evaluate", which of these is a key idea?
o: Practise muting and unmuting others politely.
Speed: a video call needs roughly 2 to 4 Mbit/s each way.
Keep water and a spare charger within reach.
Log the fault and cure.

questions.q: In "Measure and improve Create", which of these is a key idea?
o: Light from the front; camera at eye level.
Allow chat as well as voice.
Check join success rate and drop-offs.
Fallback: turn off video, then call in by phone.
